AC-2 Given both a JSON file and a lock file, the allocator still returns one more than the highest id seen in either.
AC-3 An empty directory, and a directory that does not exist, still return 1 as they do today.
AC-4 A file whose name does not match the id pattern is ignored and never raises.
AC-5 tests/test_local_relay_protocol.py passes with the new tests added, and the repository privacy gate passes.

baseline.authority: docs/design/GOV_PO_3_APPROVED_MOVEMENT_ORCHESTRATION.md -- FROZEN, Product Owner approved 2026-09-08. It fixes that a movement id resolves to exactly one relay file, and that the worktree path and the orchestrator's state record are both derived from that id. A reissued id breaks all three at once: two movements resolve to one file, share one worktree path, and merge their accounting into one record. This movement restores that invariant at its source and changes nothing else about the protocol.
baseline.engineering_baseline: scripts/local_relay.py is the only allocator of movement ids. The repository currently holds 59 lock files beside the relay JSON files, so the lock files are a real and available record of ids already handed out.
baseline.product_baseline: Not a product change. The Java product, its collectors and its UI are untouched.
baseline.test_baseline: tests/test_local_relay_protocol.py passes on origin/main today; it was run locally on 2026-09-15 before this packet was written.
baseline.what_exists:
scripts/local_relay.py defines the allocator exactly like this, at line 325:

def _next_id(relay_dir: Path) -> int:
    if not relay_dir.is_dir():
        return 1
    best = 0
    for candidate in relay_dir.glob(f"{ID_PREFIX}*.json"):
        match = re.match(r"^NXS-LOCAL-(\d{4})-", candidate.name)
        if match:
            best = max(best, int(match.group(1)))
    return best + 1

Its only caller is in the create command, around line 457:

    next_id = _next_id(relay_dir)
    full_id = f"{ID_PREFIX}{next_id:04d}"
    slug = _slugify(args.slug or start_obj["movement"])
    target = relay_dir / f"{full_id}-{slug}.json"
    if target.exists():
        print(f"error: {target} already exists", file=sys.stderr)
        return EXIT_INVALID

The lock files sit in the same directory and are named after the relay file they lock, for example relay/NXS-LOCAL-0155-brand-nexus-wordmark.json.lock and relay/NXS-LOCAL-0178-nxs-local-0178-root-identity-and-local-a.json.lock. Note that a lock name therefore ends in .json.lock, not .lock alone, and that the id is still the first four digits after the NXS-LOCAL- prefix.

invariants: An id, once handed out, is never handed out again.
The function returns an integer and never raises on an unexpected file name.
No existing file in the relay directory is created, renamed, moved or deleted by this change.

report.objective: Stop the relay from ever reissuing a movement id that has already been used. Today the id allocator looks only at committed relay JSON files, so a movement whose JSON was never committed frees its id while its lock file, its worktree directory and its orchestrator state record all still exist under that id. On 2026-09-13 ids 0136 and 0137 were handed to two new movements; the collision was caught by hand before dispatch, and the history of the two earlier movements is gone.
output_contract: A relay that cannot hand the same movement id to two movements.
